2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this civil appeal are that the predecessor of the respondents No.1-6 as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1996 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Bochagonj, Dinajpur against the predecessor of the appellants along with others as opposite parties under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly SAT Act) for pre-emption in respect of the schedule land as appended to the petition. The petitioner's case, in a nutshell, is that the pre-emptor was the co-sharer tenant in the case holding and the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 were the strangers to the case holding. The other co-sharer tenants of the case holding, namely pre-emptees No.3 and 4 sold out the case land to the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 by two registered Kabalas No.4405 and 4406 dated 7-9-1995 without serving any notice of the transfer upon the pre-emptor and the pre-emptor came to know about the aforesaid transfer on 28-12-1995. Thereafter, on obtaining the certified copies of the Kabalas the pre-emptor filed the Miscellaneous Case for pre-emption on 12-2-1996. 

 3. The pre-emptees No.3(Ka)-3(Ga) and 4 contested the case by filing separate written objections denying all the material facts stated in the averments of the petition. The contentions made in both the written objections are more or less the same. Their case, in brief, is that the pre-emptees No.3 and 4 having been the owners of the case land by way of inheritance and Hiba-bil-Ewaz, mortgaged the same to the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 in need of money at a nominal consideration value by two registered Kabalas dated 7-9-1995 on condition to re-convey the same and accordingly the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 re-conveyed the case land in favour of the pre-emptee No.4 due to the demise of pre-emptee No.3 by registered deeds No.199 and 200 dated 11-1-1997 and the pre-emptee No.4 had been possessing the case land since then and, as such, the case of the pre-emptor was not maintainable and it was liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 11. OPW1 stated in his deposition that the pre-emptees No.3 and 4 took loan from the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 and the case land was transferred to the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 in consideration of Taka 6,000 and while execution of the sale deeds there was condition for re-conveyance and Ekrarnama deeds were also executed on the day of sale. There was a condition in the deeds that the said loan money should return by 29th Poush, 1403 BS. He stated further that subsequently he and her wife executed re-conveyance deed in favour of the pre-emptees No.3-4 after repayment of loan money. He stated further that due to the 'death of pre-emptee No.3 the re-conveyance deed had been executed in the name of pre-emptee No.4. 

 12. Pre-emptee No.4 had been examined as OPW4, who identified the said re-conveyance deeds, which were marked as Exhibits-Gha and Uma. OPW4 stated in his testimony that his father transferred the case land to the pre-emptees No.1 and 2 for household needs and the total value in those deed was Taka 6,000. Subsequently he got back the case land on 27th day of Poush, 1403 BS corresponding to 11-1-1997 of the Gregorian calendar. He also repaid the whole loan money. The case land is in his possession. 

 13. OPWs 2, 3, 6 and 7 are the witnesses, who knew about the said sale. OPW 2 stated in his testimony that the case land was sold on condition of re-conveyance, subsequently the loan money was repaid, and thereafter the case land was re-conveyed to the vendor. A. Baki (pre-emptee No.4) is in possession of the case land. 

 15. OPW 5 was present at the time of execution of the sale deeds as well as re-conveyance deeds. He stated in his deposition that he was present at the time of execution of sale deed as well as re-conveyance deed. On re-payment of Taka 6,000 the possession of the case land was returned to the pre-emptee No.4 and the case land is in his (pre-emptee No.4) possession.
